scope: Generic block-shape audit only; no source edits, build, or tests performed.

coverage.interpretation: The comparison is exhaustive over all 32,366 enumerated states, not only the candidate subset: each state has a status, and the 17,090 shape_index candidates equal all static mismatches in the comparison. The remaining 15,231 compared states match both channels. Candidate/difference means computed-vs-oracle discrepancy, not a proven player-visible or live-game bug. The separate 45 statuses are context-dependent and are not static mismatches.

largest_shared_families_and_examples.family: Unmodeled/special outline shapes, especially non-colliding plants, wires, fire, rails, controls, banners, coral, etc.
largest_shared_families_and_examples.evidence: outline-only differences dominate: 14,511 states; examples redstone_wire 1,296, fire 512, wall families 322 states each, tripwire 128, glow_lichen/resin_clump/sculk_vein 126 each. These are often currently full-cube outline fallback despite empty collision.
largest_shared_families_and_examples.sample: redstone_wire with east/north/south/west connections up/side has empty collision and vanilla outline composed of 1/16- and 1/16..1.0 wire parts; current outline is the full [0,0,0,1,1,1] cube.
largest_shared_families_and_examples.likely_effect: Can make interaction raycasts hit broad invisible regions or make small/non-colliding blocks targetable as full cubes; this is a code-level discrepancy, not proof of a reported live bug.

largest_shared_families_and_examples.family: Walls and wall-like connection shapes; existing wall_shape ignores vanilla outline height cap.
largest_shared_families_and_examples.evidence: Many stone/resin/deepslate/sulfur/cinnabar wall IDs each have 322 outline differences. Existing wall_shape is used as collision and fallback outline; on a sample no-connections wall it returns central post y=0..1.5, while oracle outline is y=0..1.0. Connected arms also need low/tall-specific outline heights and vanilla post/arm unions.
largest_shared_families_and_examples.sample: cobblestone_wall, east/north/south/west=none, up=true, waterlogged=true: collision central box [0.25,0,0.25,0.75,1.5,0.75]; outline [0.25,0,0.25,0.75,1,0.75].

largest_shared_families_and_examples.family: Existing handlers with wrong/incomplete properties or missing state branches.
largest_shared_families_and_examples.evidence: copper_bars (all eight oxidation/wax families) have 256 combined state differences; existing generic _pane condition only handles names ending _pane, while _bars only handles iron_bars. open fence gates are correctly no-collision but their nonempty outline is missed (oak_fence_gate family 32 states per wood; open north sample oracle outline [0,0,0.375,1,0.8125,0.625], current empty). Copper/regular rails and buttons share this risk; controls need their actual outline tables, not cube fallback.

largest_shared_families_and_examples.family: Small collision exceptions to prioritize separately from outline-only coverage.

Other frequent collision+outline clusters include repeater (64), calibrated_sculk_sensor (384), copper_bars variants, heads, lights, and block entities.

context_dependent_detail.moving_piston: 12 states; collision/outline depends on moving piston/entity progress and carried block state, so a single state-id shape table cannot reproduce runtime shape. Needs world/entity context and interpolation if exactness is desired.
context_dependent_detail.scaffolding: 32 states; comparison marks collision/outline context-dependent (neighbor/support context), not an ordinary state-property-only lookup. Preserve contextual path or intentionally accept a documented approximation.
context_dependent_detail.powder_snow: 1 state; entity-context collision (e.g. entity ability/boots) must not be conflated with static shape. Keep entity-dependent decision at collision call site.

root_cause_and_minimal_recommendation.current_flow: pomme-client/src/physics/block_shape.rs::compute_shape/compute_outline derive partial geometry from hand-coded id/property branches; unhandled shapes become None. pomme-client/src/world/block/mod.rs::build_table (around lines 400-430) computes these per state and stores BlockData.shape/outline. partial_shape falls back to an empty slice when has_collision=false, while outline_shape falls back to a full cube. Thus a noncolliding small outline needs an explicit compute_outline entry; a collision shape needs compute_shape; a collision-vs-outline difference needs both.
root_cause_and_minimal_recommendation.root_issue: A hand-maintained partial family allowlist is serving as a universal shape oracle. Unhandled state-dependent shapes silently become full cube for outline and full cube for collidable collision. The discrepancy is broad coverage debt, not one shared coordinate bug.
root_cause_and_minimal_recommendation.recommended_change: Use the existing per-version vanilla shape capture/generation approach rather than growing match arms or adding a giant Rust hardcode. Extend the current vanilla-driven generator pipeline (tools/stategen/StateDump.java plus tools/blockgen/src/main.rs, or a small sibling shape dumper/compactor) to emit each state’s static collision and outline AABBs keyed in the same dense state-id order as blocks-<version>.json; deduplicate equal shapes and encode each block as default shape index plus sparse state-offset overrides (or a compact per-state index array when denser). Embed generated compact shape data next to blocks-<version>.json, decode once in build_table into the existing BlockData.shape/outline fields, and retain contextual handlers exclusively for the 45 marked states. For every generated dataset validate version, block/state counts and state-order alignment before use. If staged instead of wholesale, first add outline data for small noncolliding shapes and accurate wall outline; then prioritize actual collision discrepancies separately.
root_cause_and_minimal_recommendation.minimal_runtime_contract: Continue representing None as full cube, Some([]) as empty, and Some(boxes) as explicit geometry. Populate the exact static per-state shapes before BlockData construction; do not alter has_collision semantics to manufacture collision. Keep context-dependent collision decisions outside this static table. Avoid runtime parsing of a giant oracle JSON; generated compact embedded indices and shared box dictionary are preferable.
root_cause_and_minimal_recommendation.existing_vanilla_data_reuse: third_party/SteelMC/steel-registry/build_assets/blocks.json already contains vanilla-derived collision_shapes, outline_shapes, support_shapes, occlusion_shapes and an interned global shapes dictionary with per-block overwrites; it is an immediately reusable oracle for the available registry version and existing tests already compare selected cases to it. It is 20,132,079 bytes and is not the client’s current embedded per-version shape table, so include_str!/runtime-parsing it wholesale is not a sensible shipped solution and it does not establish coverage for every protocol table. Existing pomme-client/src/world/block/data/blocks-<version>.json (e.g. 26.2: 172,683 bytes) supplies IDs/properties only; state-<version>.json (26.2: 310,990 bytes) supplies baked light/collision flag fields, not AABBs. A vanilla Java dump/compact generation step per supported version is the correct reuse path; do not mistake the Steel registry oracle’s current single generated data for all 13 embedded versions.
